claims.text: AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.

In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, the stage lock only protects an execution once it is actually running; a newer execution can still overtake an execution that is waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping it before it ever starts.

If a CodePipeline CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment rather than colliding with one already in progress (under the default `SUPERSEDED` execution mode).
The AWS CodePipeline user guide page 'concepts-how-it-works' documents CodePipeline's execution modes, including the default `SUPERSEDED` mode.

Setting an AWS CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue so each one runs in turn, rather than a later commit superseding an earlier execution that never got its turn.
The AWS CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType` V2).
To use `QUEUED` execution mode, both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` must be set when defining the pipeline, including via the AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.

The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource is described in a section below on the same page ('Manage the pipeline with Pulumi'), and the link target /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ exists.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment (targeted by a deployment job) that can prevent concurrent runs from reaching the same stack.
The page links to an 'update conflict' troubleshooting page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ that documents update conflicts.
In Azure DevOps, an exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is set at the stage level (on the stage that references the environment with the exclusive lock check).
The Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` stage property accepts the values `sequential` and `runLatest`, and `runLatest` is the default.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts inputs `command: up`, `stack`, and `args` (e.g., `args: --yes`).

With Azure Pipelines exclusive lock `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the lock, so an older run waiting behind it is passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With Azure Pipelines exclusive lock `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud itself serializes updates to a stack, one at a time.
`runLatest` is acceptable for a preview environment where only the newest state matters, but not for a stack where every update needs to land.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The registry page /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exists for the `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource.
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent runs reach the same Pulumi stack, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available (no limit on simultaneously running builds).
The link target /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ (update conflict page) exists in the Pulumi docs.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds", located under the configuration's General Settings.
The default value of TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" option is 0, meaning unlimited.

Setting TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first and run only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior for a stack.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment that the deployment job targets serializes Pulumi deployments (prevents concurrent runs against the same stack).
In Azure Pipelines, the exclusive lock check should be paired with `lockBehavior: sequential` set on the stage so that runs queue in order.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section anchored '#serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's pipeline execution mode has a `QUEUED` value.
The default AWS CodePipeline execution mode is SUPERSEDED, in which a newer execution supersedes an older execution that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section anchored '#serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, setting the build configuration's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option to `1` serializes Pulumi deployments.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section anchored '#limit-concurrent-builds' (the TeamCity guide).
